title: Operations-Research Queueing Model for Human-Audit Throughput

original_idea.body:
# Operations-Research Queueing Model for Human-Audit Throughput Under Load

**Problem:** Human-in-the-loop audit is a bottleneck: if monitors flag faster than humans review, a queue builds and dangerous actions execute unreviewed. Control designs rarely model this.

**Direction:** Import queueing theory (M/M/c, priority queues). Model flagged actions as arrivals into a finite reviewer queue, parameterize from flag rates and review times, and compute the probability an action executes before review at various staffing and threshold levels.

**Why it matters:** Quantifies the human-oversight bottleneck and yields concrete staffing/threshold guidance. Pure modeling, no compute.

**Relevant context:** Queueing theory (Erlang, M/M/c); Ctrl-Z (arXiv:2504.10374); arXiv:2511.02997.
